steps.title: Cost price and selling price
steps.content: Cost price (CP) is what the shopkeeper pays. Selling price (SP) is what the customer pays. Profit happens when SP is greater than CP; loss happens when SP is smaller than CP.
steps.tip: Always calculate profit or loss from CP, not from SP.

steps.title: Calculate the profit
steps.prompt: An item costs ₹800 and sells for ₹920. What is the profit?

steps.title: Convert profit into a percentage
steps.content: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. The cost price is the base in both formulas.
steps.formula:
Profit % = ((SP − CP) / CP) × 100
Loss % = ((CP − SP) / CP) × 100

steps.title: Find the loss percentage
steps.prompt: A phone is bought for ₹1,200 and sold for ₹1,080. What is the loss percentage?

steps.title: Reverse the selling price
steps.content: If CP and profit percentage are known, SP = CP × (100 + profit%)/100. For a loss, SP = CP × (100 − loss%)/100.
steps.tip: For successive discounts, calculate each discount on the current price, not always on the original price.

questions.prompt: CP is ₹600 and SP is ₹690. What is the profit percentage?
An item is sold for ₹840 at a loss of 16%. Find its cost price.
A trader gains 25% on an item whose CP is ₹480. Find SP.
A product is sold for ₹540 after a 10% loss. Find CP.
Which value is the base when calculating profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage is profit divided by cost price, multiplied by 100.
